title: Speaking Part 1 — one question, one card
note: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.
The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.
That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

note.question: Where are you from?
alts: I'm from ___, and I've lived here my whole life. I really love it, mainly because ___ — and ___. Most evenings ___.
A simple question, a simple shape: say it, say why, then one picture of your life there.
a
I'm from Funchal, and I've lived here my whole life.
my whole life
r
I really love it, mainly because it feels safe and relaxed — and the weather's amazing almost all year round.
mainly because
almost all year round
I'm from Funchal, which is the capital of Madeira.
Funchal is a city with approximately 100,000 inhabitants.
A fact from Wikipedia, not a reason. The examiner wants why YOU like it.
e
Most evenings my friends and I sit on the wall by the marina and watch the cruise ships leave.
Most evenings
watch the cruise ships leave
For example, Funchal has lots of nice places.
Vague. One place, one habit, one picture.
Many cruise ships visit Funchal every year.
A statistic in disguise. What do YOU do?
Well, it's a bit complicated, actually. I was born in ___, but ___ when I was ___. So I'd say I'm from ___ now — although ___!
A 'complicated' answer is a gift in Part 1: the contrast at the end shows you can hold two ideas at once.
x
Well, it's a bit complicated, actually.
it's a bit complicated
That is an interesting question.
I am from Venezuela and Madeira.
That's the answer, and it skips the reaction. Show the question made you think first.
a
I was born in Venezuela, but my family moved back to Madeira when I was five.
moved back
when I was five
c
So I'd say I'm from Funchal now — although when my grandma makes arepas, I feel totally Venezuelan!
So I'd say
although when
So I'm from Funchal and I like it very much.
No turn. 'Although' should swing back to the other side of you.
However, many Madeirans emigrated to Venezuela in the past.
History lesson. The contrast should be about you, not the island.
I'm from ___, a ___ just outside ___. It's the kind of place where ___. Last week ___, and ___!
No reaction, straight in — then one tiny story proves the 'everyone knows you' idea instead of just saying it.
a
I'm from Câmara de Lobos, a fishing town just outside Funchal.
just outside
e
It's the kind of place where everyone knows you. Last week I forgot my wallet at the bakery, and the owner just told my mum when she walked past!
It's the kind of place where
Last week
just told my mum
For example, it has many restaurants and shops.
A list, not a moment. What happened, to you, once?
It is famous because Winston Churchill painted there.
True, and interesting — but it's a guidebook fact, not your example.

note.question: What's your home like?
alts: We live in a ___ in ___, on the ___ floor, so we've got ___. The only downside is that ___, which drives me crazy.
Describe it, then complain a little. A small 'but' makes a description sound like a real opinion.
a
We live in a flat in São Martinho, on the fourth floor, so we've got a great view of the sea.
so we've got
c
The only downside is that it's quite small, so I have to share a room with my little brother, which drives me crazy.
The only downside is that
which drives me crazy
Also, it has two bathrooms and a kitchen.
'Also' adds another fact. A contrast turns the other way.
Nevertheless, the apartment presents certain disadvantages.
Oh, it's pretty ___, to be honest. It's my ___' house up in ___, with ___. It's ___ in winter, but I wouldn't swap it for ___.
The reaction warns the examiner there's a story. 'I wouldn't swap it' shows affection without saying 'I love it'.
x
Oh, it's pretty old, to be honest.
to be honest
My house is an old house.
Flat and repetitive. React with a feeling, not a label.
Well, that's a good question.
a
It's my grandparents' house up in Santo António, with a big garden full of banana trees and chickens.
full of
c
It's freezing in winter, but I wouldn't swap it for a modern flat.
I wouldn't swap it for
It's freezing in winter, and it's also very old.
Two complaints in a row. The 'but' needs to swing back to what you love.
In contrast, modern flats have central heating.
About flats in general, not about your home.
It's a ___ house, nothing special, but ___ is my favourite place in the world. It's the only place where I can ___. Last month ___, and ___!
'Nothing special, but…' is a lovely move: lower expectations, then surprise. The example makes it funny.
a
It's a normal house, nothing special, but my bedroom is my favourite place in the world.
nothing special, but
r
It's the only place where I can shut the door, put my music on and just be myself.
It's the only place where
just be myself
My bedroom is my favourite room in the house.
Bedrooms are important for teenagers' mental health.
A magazine headline. Say why it matters to you.
e
Last month I painted one wall dark blue, and my mum still hasn't forgiven me.
Last month
still hasn't forgiven me
For example, I have a bed and a desk.
An inventory, not a moment.
I like the colour blue very much.
A preference, not an example. What happened?

note.question: Who are you most like in your family?
alts: I'm definitely most like my ___. We both love ___, and we can ___ for hours. Last summer we ___. The big difference is that she's ___, and I'm… well, not!
Answer, one shared moment, then the difference. The joke at the end is the contrast.
a
I'm definitely most like my mum. We both love being outside, and we can chat for hours.
most like
We both
for hours
e
Last summer we did a levada walk together and talked the entire way.
the entire way
For example, we are both very similar.
Levadas are irrigation channels built centuries ago.
A guidebook fact. The example is what you two did.
c
The big difference is that she's really patient, and I'm… well, not!
The big difference is that
And she's also really kind and friendly.
More similarities. The contrast has to show a difference.
However, personality is influenced by many factors.
Ha — everyone says my ___, and it's so annoying. We've got the same ___, the same ___ and the same ___. Mind you, if I'm honest, I'd rather be like ___ than anyone else.
An annoyed reaction, then a soft ending that contradicts it. That change of heart is what sounds fourteen.
x
Ha — everyone says my dad, and it's so annoying.
everyone says
I am most similar to my father.
That's the answer, stated stiffly. The reaction is how you feel about it.
That is an interesting question.
a
We've got the same laugh, the same terrible jokes and the same obsession with Marítimo.
the same
obsession with
c
Mind you, if I'm honest, I'd rather be like him than anyone else.
Mind you
if I'm honest
I'd rather
Mind you, he also supports Marítimo.
That's another similarity. 'Mind you' should turn the answer.
On the other hand, my mother is also nice.
Changes the subject instead of turning the feeling.
Hmm, probably my ___, actually. She ___ when I was little, and she taught me ___ before I could even ___. We're both quite ___, but we ___.
A hesitation, a surprising answer, a detail with a comparison in it. The reason is about character, not appearance.
x
Hmm, probably my grandma, actually.
probably
actually
Definitely, one hundred per cent, my grandma!
Too certain for a surprising answer. 'Probably… actually' sounds like you're thinking.
Well, that's a good question.
a
She moved in with us when I was little, and she taught me to cook before I could even ride a bike.
moved in with us
before I could even
r
We're both quite quiet, but we notice everything. My family calls us 'the detectives'.
We're both
but we notice everything
She taught me to cook when I was young.
Grandparents play an important role in Portuguese families.
A sociology point. Why are YOU like her?

note.question: Do you go on holiday with your family?
alts: Yes, but we usually stay on the island. Last summer we spent ___ in ___ and ___ every day. We don't go abroad very often, because ___.
Answer, one real holiday, then the honest 'but'. That's the shape of your B2 column, without the stray 'here's.
a
Yes, but we usually stay on the island.
usually
e
Last summer we spent a week in Porto Moniz and swam in the natural pools every day.
Last summer
every day
For example, we go on holiday in Madeira.
Porto Moniz is in the north-west of the island.
Geography, not a memory.
c
We don't go abroad very often, because flights from here are so expensive.
very often
so expensive
We also go to the beach a lot.
Adds, doesn't turn.
Nevertheless, domestic tourism has several advantages.
Not as much as I'd like to! My parents both work in ___, so ___ is their busiest time. So we go away in ___ instead — which sounds weird, but at least ___.
'Not as much as I'd like' is a reaction and an answer in one. The 'weird, but' ending turns a complaint into something good.
x
Not as much as I'd like to!
as much as I'd like
No.
A closed door. React with the feeling behind it.
Holidays are important for families.
A general statement, not a reaction.
a
My parents both work in hotels, so summer is their busiest time.
their busiest time
c
So we go away in November instead — which sounds weird, but at least the beaches in Porto Santo are completely empty.
which sounds weird, but
at least
So we don't go on holiday in summer.
However, the hotel industry is essential to Madeira's economy.
True, but now you're writing an essay about tourism.
Yeah, every ___ we fly to ___ to see ___. It's the only time the whole family is together, so it's ___ but ___. Last year ___, and ___!
Reason plus a funny example. The example does the proving — you don't need to say 'it's chaotic', you show it.
a
Yeah, every August we fly to Lisbon to see my cousins.
every August
r
It's the only time the whole family is together, so it's chaotic but amazing.
the whole family
chaotic but amazing
We go to Lisbon because my cousins live in Lisbon.
Circular — it repeats the answer.
Lisbon is a beautiful and historic city.
About Lisbon, not about why the trip matters.
e
Last year there were fourteen of us in one flat, and we had to take turns in the shower!
Last year
take turns
For example, we visit lots of places in Lisbon.
Vague. One moment you could film.
My cousins are the same age as me.
A fact, not a moment.

note.question: Who do you spend time with at the weekend?
alts: My ___, mostly — it's a very Madeiran thing! Every Sunday we have ___ at ___. It can get a bit ___, to be honest, but I'd really miss it if ___.
A reaction with a smile, a fact, then a mixed feeling. 'I'd miss it if we stopped' is a second conditional doing emotional work.
x
My family, mostly — it's a very Madeiran thing!
mostly
a very Madeiran thing
I spend time with my family here at weekends.
Your table's version — but the stray 'here' is a habit to avoid, and it's the answer, not a reaction.
That is an interesting question.
a
Every Sunday we have a massive lunch at my grandparents' house in Câmara de Lobos.
Every Sunday
massive
c
It can get a bit boring, to be honest, but I'd really miss it if we stopped.
It can get a bit
I'd really miss it if
It's also really delicious and fun.
No turn. Where's the other side?
However, some teenagers prefer to spend time with friends.
About 'some teenagers', not you.
My friends, definitely. On ___ we meet at ___ and just ___ for hours. It sounds pointless, but it's the only time we can ___. Last Saturday we ___ and bought absolutely nothing.
'It sounds pointless, but…' defends your answer before the examiner can judge it. The example is a punchline.
a
My friends, definitely. On Saturdays we meet at Forum Madeira and just walk around for hours.
definitely
for hours
r
It sounds pointless, but it's the only time we can talk without our parents listening.
It sounds pointless, but
without our parents listening
We go to Forum Madeira because it's a shopping centre.
Obvious. Why do you go?
Shopping centres are popular places for young people.
A general fact, not your reason.
e
Last Saturday we spent three hours there and bought absolutely nothing.
absolutely nothing
For example, there are many shops there.
About the place, not about a Saturday.
We like shopping very much.
A feeling, not a moment.
It depends on the weekend. Every other Saturday I stay with my ___ in ___, because ___. It used to feel strange, but now I actually like ___!
'Used to… but now' tells a change in one breath. Serious content, light ending — that's complex without being heavy.
x
It depends on the weekend.
It depends
I spend time with different people.
Vague, and it isn't a reaction. 'It depends' buys time naturally.
Well, that's a good question.
a
Every other Saturday I stay with my dad in Machico, because my parents are separated.
Every other Saturday
c
It used to feel strange, but now I actually like having two homes — double the birthday presents!
It used to feel
but now I actually
It is strange to have two homes.
Stops at the hard part. The 'but now' is what shows how you feel today.
Divorce is increasingly common in modern society.
An essay sentence. Keep it about you.

note: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.
The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.
That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.
Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.
No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.
About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.
A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.
Flat. A reaction shows how the question makes you feel.
Honestly? It's ___, but it's never ___. ___'s squeezed between ___ and ___, so wherever you go, ___. The only thing is, in ___ the centre gets packed with ___.
A quick opinion, a picture, then the downside. Three moves, three different jobs.
Honestly? It's small, but it's never boring.
My city is a city in Madeira.
Funchal's squeezed between the mountains and the sea, so wherever you go, you've got an amazing view.
The only thing is, in summer the centre gets packed with tourists, and walking anywhere takes ages.
Also, there are many beautiful gardens.
However, tourism has both advantages and disadvantages.
It's pretty ___, to be honest — I live in ___, not ___. It's right next to ___, but you stop noticing after a while. Mind you, when ___, half the town ___!
No reaction, straight in. The reason explains the noise; the example turns an annoyance into a local show.
It's pretty quiet, to be honest — I live in Machico, not Funchal.
It's right next to the airport, but you stop noticing after a while.
you stop noticing after a while
Machico is a quiet town in the east.
Mind you, when it's windy and the planes can't land, half the town goes out to watch!
For example, many planes land there.
Madeira airport has a famous runway.
Oh, I love it, but I'm biased! ___ feels like a big city and a village at the same time. Like, you can ___ in the evening, and the next morning ___.
One clever idea — city and village at once — proved by one tiny scene.
Oh, I love it, but I'm biased!
Funchal feels like a big city and a village at the same time.
Like, you can go to a concert in the evening, and the next morning the man at the bakery asks you how it was.
For example, there are many shops and cafés.
Where's the best place to go with friends in your city?
Definitely ___. It's ___ right by ___. It's cheap, it's ___, and there's always ___. Last summer we went almost every day, and we'd stay until ___.
Answer, three quick reasons in one breath, then a memory that proves it.
Definitely the Lido. It's a big outdoor pool right by the sea.
It's cheap, it's close to the centre, and there's always someone from school there.
The Lido is a swimming pool in Funchal.
Swimming is good exercise for teenagers.
Last summer we went almost every day, and we'd stay until they literally closed the gates.
For example, we go there a lot.
The Lido was renovated a few years ago.
Ha — anywhere with free Wi-Fi! No, seriously, we usually end up at ___. It's not exactly ___, but it's ___, and nobody ___.
A joke first, then 'No, seriously' — the move that turns a joke into a real answer.
The best place is a shopping centre.
That's the answer, and it skips the fun. React first.
No, seriously, we usually end up at Forum Madeira, in the food court.
It's not exactly exciting, but it's warm when it rains, the chips are cheap, and nobody tells us to leave.
It's also very big and modern.
However, shopping centres are bad for local shops.
The ___, especially ___. We sit on ___ and just talk for hours. Last Friday we ___ and made up funny stories about ___.
No reaction, no reason: the place and one evening there. Sometimes two moves are enough.
The seafront, especially around sunset. We sit on the wall by the marina and just talk for hours.
Last Friday we watched a huge cruise ship leave and made up funny stories about all the passengers on board.
For example, the seafront is very beautiful.
Many cruise ships visit Funchal every year.
Is there anything you'd change about your city?
Yes, I'd definitely improve ___. They're often ___, and ___ is so ___ that ___ isn't really an option. Last week I waited ___ and missed ___.
Answer, reason, and a small disaster as proof. The second conditional ('I'd') is doing the work.
Yes, I'd definitely improve the buses.
They're often late, and some of the hills are so steep that walking isn't really an option.
The buses need to be better.
Public transport is essential in modern cities.
Last week I waited forty minutes in São Martinho and missed the start of my Maths test.
For example, buses are sometimes late.
That's the reason again. One day, one bus, one consequence.
The buses in Funchal are yellow.
Hmm, just one thing, really. I'd make more places for ___, like ___. At the moment there's loads for ___, but if you're ___, there's not much to do ___.
'At the moment… but if you're fourteen' — the contrast is between two groups of people, and you're in one of them.
Yes, I would change many things.
Not a reaction, and it promises a list you won't give.
I'd make more places for teenagers, like a skate park or a youth club.
At the moment there's loads for tourists, but if you're fourteen, there's not much to do in the evenings.
Nevertheless, the city offers many facilities.
Honestly? Not much. I'd just ___ at weekends. It's the prettiest part of ___, with ___, but it's impossible to enjoy it properly with ___.
'Not much' — then one precise change. A small, specific answer sounds more confident than a long list.
Closes the door. 'Not much' leaves room for one idea.
I'd just ban cars from the old town at weekends.
It's the prettiest part of Funchal, with all the painted doors and little cafés, but it's impossible to enjoy it properly with traffic everywhere.
I'd ban cars because I don't like cars.
Cars cause pollution in many cities.
Do you travel far every day?
Not really, I'm lucky! I take ___ to my school in ___, and it only takes about ___. Although in the morning it's so ___ that I usually have to ___.
'I'm lucky' is a reaction with a smile. 'Although… so packed that' turns it around neatly.
The answer, not a reaction. How do you feel about it?
I take the bus to my school in the centre, and it only takes about twenty-five minutes.
Although in the morning it's so packed that I usually have to stand the whole way.
Although the bus is quite comfortable.
However, traffic is a problem in many cities.
Yeah, quite far, actually — I live in ___, and my school's in ___. My parents wanted me to go to a school with ___, so I don't really mind. Mind you, last week I ___!
A long journey needs a reason, and the example makes it funny instead of a complaint.
Yeah, quite far, actually — I live in Camacha, and my school's in Funchal.
My parents wanted me to go to a school with a good music programme, so I don't really mind.
It's far because Camacha is far from Funchal.
Circular — the geography isn't a reason.
Many students travel long distances to school.
Mind you, last week I fell asleep on the bus and woke up at the very last stop!
For example, the bus takes fifty minutes.
Camacha is famous for wicker baskets.
Oh, no — I'm really lucky. I just walk. My school's only about ___ from my flat. The only problem is that it's all ___, so I arrive every morning looking like ___.
Short journey, short answer — and a funny image at the end so it doesn't die.
A closed door. Show a feeling.
I just walk. My school's only about ten minutes from my flat.
The only problem is that it's all uphill, so I arrive every morning looking like I've run a marathon.
And the walk is really nice.
However, walking is healthier than driving.
Do you prefer going by car or by public transport?
I definitely prefer ___. The bus is ___ and ___, and I can ___ on the way. The only downside is that it's sometimes ___, especially when ___.
Your B2 answer, cleaned up: answer, two reasons joined naturally, and an honest downside.
The bus is cheaper and better for the environment, and I can chat to my friends on the way.
I prefer the bus to the car.
Public transport reduces carbon emissions significantly.
The only downside is that it's sometimes late, especially when it's windy along the coast.
Also, the bus drivers are friendly.
However, cars are more popular in Madeira.
___, no question. My dad drives me to ___. With my ___ and my ___, the bus would be a nightmare, and it takes twice as long.
A firm reaction, then a reason that's pure logistics. 'Would be a nightmare' — the conditional does the imagining.
Too weak for how sure the rest of the answer is.
My dad drives me to football training twice a week, and to matches at the weekend.
With my kit bag and my boots, the bus would be a nightmare, and it takes twice as long.
I prefer the car because I like cars.
Cars are faster than buses in general.
Hmm, it depends. For short trips I'd rather ___, because it's more ___. But if we're going up to ___, like ___, the car's the only real option.
'It depends' — then both sides, each with a reason. A classic B2 balance in three sentences.
For short trips I'd rather take the bus, because it's more relaxing and I can listen to music.
But if we're going up to the mountains, like Pico do Arieiro, the car's the only real option.
But the bus is also relaxing.
However, cars are expensive to maintain.
What do you usually do in the evenings?
I usually do my homework ___. If I leave it too late, I just ___. But on ___ I always ___.
Routine, reason, and the exception. Exceptions make routines sound real.
I usually do my homework straight after dinner.
If I leave it too late, I just get really tired and can't concentrate at all.
If I leave it too late
I do my homework because I have homework.
But on Fridays I always meet my friends for a walk along the seafront.
And then I go to bed.
However, some students prefer to study in the morning.
Ha — mostly ___! We've only got one ___, and she always wants to ___. Mind you, I secretly ___, but I'd never tell her that.
A funny reaction, the situation, then a confession. 'I'd never tell her that' is pure fourteen.
Ha — mostly arguing with my sister about the TV!
In the evenings I watch television.
We've only got one in the living room, and she always wants to watch reality shows.
Mind you, I secretly enjoy them too, but I'd never tell her that.
Mind you, she's older than me.
However, reality shows are not educational.
I help my ___ cook dinner most evenings. She gets home really late from ___, so it's kind of our special time together. Last night we made ___ together, and I nearly ___!
A warm reason — 'our time together' — and a funny disaster to prove it's real.
I help my mum cook dinner most evenings.
She gets home really late from the hospital, so it's kind of our special time together.
I help her because she asks me.
True, maybe, but it misses the feeling.
Cooking is a useful skill for young people.
Last night we made espetada together, and I nearly set the whole kitchen on fire!
For example, we cook many different dishes.
Espetada is a traditional Madeiran dish.
Do you get a lot of homework?
Oh, way too much! We get quite a lot every week, especially in ___ and ___. I try to do it as soon as I get home, though, because I hate ___.
A dramatic reaction, a calmer answer, then 'though' — the contrast sits at the end of the sentence, like in speech.
We get quite a lot every week, especially in Maths and English.
I try to do it as soon as I get home, though, because I hate leaving it until the last minute.
as soon as I get home
Not really, to be honest. Our teachers prefer ___, so we get ___ instead of ___. The problem is, I always leave it until ___, and then I ___.
A surprising 'no', a reason, and an honest admission. Admitting a bad habit sounds very natural.
Our teachers prefer projects, so we get one big task every few weeks instead of homework every day.
I don't get a lot because I don't get much.
The problem is, I always leave it until the night before, and then I panic.
It depends on the week. Usually it's fine, to be honest, but in the weeks before ___ it's absolutely crazy. Last month I had ___ in ___, and I was studying until ___ every single night.
'It depends' — then the example shows exactly what 'crazy' means.
Vague, and it isn't really a reaction.
Usually it's fine, to be honest, but in the weeks before exams it's absolutely crazy.
Last month I had three tests in four days, and I was studying until midnight every single night.
For example, we have many tests.
Is there something you do every week after school?
Yes, I play ___ at school ___, after classes. It's a great way to ___ after ___. The only thing is that I'm always ___ afterwards, so I ___.
Your B2 answer: routine, reason, and a funny cost at the end.
Yes, I play football at school twice a week, after classes.
It's a great way to relax after sitting down in class all day.
I play football because I like football.
Sport is important for teenagers' health.
The only thing is that I'm always exhausted afterwards, so I do my homework half asleep.
And I also play at the weekend.
However, too much sport can cause injuries.
Yeah — ___ lessons, every ___. I've been learning the ___ — it's a ___, a bit like ___. Last Christmas I played ___ at ___, and my grandad, who's really tough, actually ___.
Present perfect continuous ('I've been learning'), a tiny explanation for the examiner, and a moving moment.
I've been learning the braguinha — it's a tiny Madeiran guitar, a bit like a ukulele.
Last Christmas I played a solo at the school concert, and my grandad, who's really tough, actually cried.
For example, I practise every week.
The braguinha is the ancestor of the ukulele.
Every ___ I go to ___ — we meet in ___. It sounds a bit old-fashioned, but it's how I ___. Last month we ___ at ___, and it was so ___ we ___.
'It sounds old-fashioned, but…' defends your answer. The example is a mini adventure.
Every Friday I go to the scouts — we meet in a hall near my school.
It sounds a bit old-fashioned, but it's how I made most of my friends.
It sounds a bit old-fashioned, but
I go to the scouts because it's on Fridays.
Not a reason, just a timetable.
Last month we camped at Fanal, and it was so foggy we got lost for an hour.
For example, we do many activities.
Fanal is a forest in the north-west.
What are you going to do this weekend?
This weekend I'm going to ___ with ___. We're taking ___, because ___ — and we deserve it after ___. The only problem is that my friend ___ is scared of ___!
Future plans ('I'm going to', 'We're taking'), a reason, and a funny problem.
This weekend I'm going to Cabo Girão with some friends.
We're taking a picnic, because the view is amazing — and we deserve it after our exams.
We're going because we want to go.
Cabo Girão is one of the highest cliffs in Europe.
The only problem is that my friend Rita is scared of heights!
And the weather will be nice.
Nothing exciting, I'm afraid. My ___'s coming from ___, so we're having ___ on ___. Actually, I'm quite looking forward to it — she always ___.
A modest reaction, then 'Actually' — the turn that changes your own mind in front of the examiner.
My cousin's coming from Lisbon, so we're having a big family lunch at my grandparents' house on Sunday.
Actually, I'm quite looking forward to it — she always brings the best gossip from the city.
However, family lunches can be long.
Ooh, something I've been waiting for all year! It's ___, so I'm going to watch ___ on ___. Last year my little sister was in it, dressed as ___, and she refused to ___.
An excited reaction, the plan, then a funny memory from last year.
Ooh, something I've been waiting for all year!
That's the answer, not a reaction.
It's the Flower Festival, so I'm going to watch the parade in the centre.
Last year my little sister was in it, dressed as a tulip, and she refused to take the costume off for a week.
For example, there are many flowers.
The Flower Festival happens every spring.
Not at all! I set ___ every morning, and I still only just ___. Weirdly, though, at the weekend I ___ without ___.
'Weirdly, though' — you notice something odd about yourself. That's what makes it sound thought, not learned.
No, I'm not a morning person.
The answer, not a reaction. Say it with feeling.
I set three alarms every morning, and I still only just catch the bus to school.
Weirdly, though, at the weekend I wake up at seven without any alarm at all, which drives me crazy.

Swimming there is so relaxing, and the water's really clear.
I like the beach because it's the beach.
The only problem is that in summer they get really crowded, so we have to get there early.
And the sand is very black.
Honestly? Absolutely nothing! I just want to ___, ___ and not think about ___. Although after about a week, I usually get bored and start ___.
An honest reaction, then a self-aware twist. 'Start annoying my parents' is funny and real.
I just want to sleep late, play games with my friends and not think about school at all.
Although after about a week, I usually get bored and start annoying my parents and my little brother.
However, holidays are important for rest.
I love exploring ___, especially on foot. Last holiday we walked ___, right at ___, and the colours of ___ were incredible. My brother complained the whole way, though!
Answer, one walk, and a funny 'though' about someone else.
I love exploring new places, especially on foot.
Last holiday we walked the São Lourenço trail, right at the eastern tip of the island, and the colours of the cliffs were incredible.
Ponta de São Lourenço is a nature reserve.
My brother complained the whole way, though!
Oh, I love it — well, the being-there part. Every summer we take ___ to ___, and the beach there just goes on forever. ___, on the other hand, is a nightmare: ___ of feeling sick.
The reaction already hints at a 'but' — and the contrast pays it off.
Oh, I love it — well, the being-there part.
Travelling is something that many people enjoy.
Every summer we take the ferry to Porto Santo, and the beach there just goes on forever.
The ferry, on the other hand, is a nightmare: two and a half hours of feeling sick.
On the other hand, Porto Santo is also beautiful.
Not really, and I blame ___. Our runway's famous for ___, so flights get ___ all the time. Last Christmas we were stuck in ___ for ___, and my little sister cried the whole time.
A surprising 'no' needs a reason fast — and the reason needs proof.
Not really, and I blame the airport.
Our runway's famous for strong winds, so flights get cancelled all the time.
I don't like travelling because I don't enjoy it.
Last Christmas we were stuck in Lisbon for two days, and my little sister cried the whole time.
For example, many flights are cancelled.
Lisbon is the capital of Portugal.
I'd love to travel more, honestly. I've only been off the island ___, both times to see ___. Flying from here is ___, and my parents hardly ever get holidays at the same time.
A wish, the facts, and an honest reason why not.
I'd love to travel more, honestly.
Travel is very important in the modern world.
I've only been off the island twice, both times to see my cousins in Jersey.
Flying from here is really expensive, and my parents hardly ever get holidays at the same time.
Travelling helps you learn about other cultures.

cards.question: Where are you from?

alts.frame: I'm from ___, and I've lived here my whole life. I really love it, mainly because ___ — and ___. Most evenings ___.
alts.why: A simple question, a simple shape: say it, say why, then one picture of your life there.

segs.t: I'm from Funchal, and I've lived here my whole life.
I really love it, mainly because it feels safe and relaxed — and the weather's amazing almost all year round.

wrong.t: I'm from Funchal, which is the capital of Madeira.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Funchal is a city with approximately 100,000 inhabitants.
wrong.why: A fact from Wikipedia, not a reason. The examiner wants why YOU like it.

segs.t: Most evenings my friends and I sit on the wall by the marina and watch the cruise ships leave.

wrong.t: For example, Funchal has lots of nice places.
wrong.why: Vague. One place, one habit, one picture.

wrong.t: Many cruise ships visit Funchal every year.
wrong.why: A statistic in disguise. What do YOU do?

alts.frame: Well, it's a bit complicated, actually. I was born in ___, but ___ when I was ___. So I'd say I'm from ___ now — although ___!
alts.why: A 'complicated' answer is a gift in Part 1: the contrast at the end shows you can hold two ideas at once.

segs.t: Well, it's a bit complicated, actually.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

wrong.t: I am from Venezuela and Madeira.
wrong.why: That's the answer, and it skips the reaction. Show the question made you think first.

segs.t: I was born in Venezuela, but my family moved back to Madeira when I was five.
So I'd say I'm from Funchal now — although when my grandma makes arepas, I feel totally Venezuelan!

wrong.t: So I'm from Funchal and I like it very much.
wrong.why: No turn. 'Although' should swing back to the other side of you.

wrong.t: However, many Madeirans emigrated to Venezuela in the past.
wrong.why: History lesson. The contrast should be about you, not the island.

alts.frame: I'm from ___, a ___ just outside ___. It's the kind of place where ___. Last week ___, and ___!
alts.why: No reaction, straight in — then one tiny story proves the 'everyone knows you' idea instead of just saying it.

segs.t: I'm from Câmara de Lobos, a fishing town just outside Funchal.
It's the kind of place where everyone knows you. Last week I forgot my wallet at the bakery, and the owner just told my mum when she walked past!
marks: It's the kind of place where

wrong.t: For example, it has many restaurants and shops.
wrong.why: A list, not a moment. What happened, to you, once?

wrong.t: It is famous because Winston Churchill painted there.
wrong.why: True, and interesting — but it's a guidebook fact, not your example.

cards.question: What's your home like?

alts.frame: We live in a ___ in ___, on the ___ floor, so we've got ___. The only downside is that ___, which drives me crazy.
alts.why: Describe it, then complain a little. A small 'but' makes a description sound like a real opinion.

segs.t: We live in a flat in São Martinho, on the fourth floor, so we've got a great view of the sea.
The only downside is that it's quite small, so I have to share a room with my little brother, which drives me crazy.

wrong.t: Also, it has two bathrooms and a kitchen.
wrong.why: 'Also' adds another fact. A contrast turns the other way.

wrong.t: Nevertheless, the apartment presents certain disadvantages.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: Oh, it's pretty ___, to be honest. It's my ___'s house up in ___, with ___. It's ___ in winter, but I wouldn't swap it for ___.
alts.why: The reaction warns the examiner there's a story. 'I wouldn't swap it' shows affection without saying 'I love it'.

segs.t: Oh, it's pretty old, to be honest.

wrong.t: My house is an old house.
wrong.why: Flat and repetitive. React with a feeling, not a label.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: It's my grandparents' house up in Santo António, with a big garden full of banana trees and chickens.
It's freezing in winter, but I wouldn't swap it for a modern flat.

wrong.t: It's freezing in winter, and it's also very old.
wrong.why: Two complaints in a row. The 'but' needs to swing back to what you love.

wrong.t: In contrast, modern flats have central heating.
wrong.why: About flats in general, not about your home.

alts.frame: It's a ___ house, nothing special, but ___ is my favourite place in the world. It's the only place where I can ___. Last month ___, and ___!
alts.why: 'Nothing special, but…' is a lovely move: lower expectations, then surprise. The example makes it funny.

segs.t: It's a normal house, nothing special, but my bedroom is my favourite place in the world.
It's the only place where I can shut the door, put my music on and just be myself.

wrong.t: My bedroom is my favourite room in the house.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Bedrooms are important for teenagers' mental health.
wrong.why: A magazine headline. Say why it matters to you.

segs.t: Last month I painted one wall dark blue, and my mum still hasn't forgiven me.

wrong.t: For example, I have a bed and a desk.
wrong.why: An inventory, not a moment.

wrong.t: I like the colour blue very much.
wrong.why: A preference, not an example. What happened?

cards.question: Who are you most like in your family?

alts.frame: I'm definitely most like my ___. We both love ___, and we can ___ for hours. Last summer we ___. The big difference is that she's ___, and I'm… well, not!
alts.why: Answer, one shared moment, then the difference. The joke at the end is the contrast.

segs.t: I'm definitely most like my mum. We both love being outside, and we can chat for hours.
Last summer we did a levada walk together and talked the entire way.

wrong.t: For example, we are both very similar.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Levadas are irrigation channels built centuries ago.
wrong.why: A guidebook fact. The example is what you two did.

segs.t: The big difference is that she's really patient, and I'm… well, not!

wrong.t: And she's also really kind and friendly.
wrong.why: More similarities. The contrast has to show a difference.

wrong.t: However, personality is influenced by many factors.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: Ha — everyone says my ___, and it's so annoying. We've got the same ___, the same ___ and the same ___. Mind you, if I'm honest, I'd rather be like ___ than anyone else.
alts.why: An annoyed reaction, then a soft ending that contradicts it. That change of heart is what sounds fourteen.

segs.t: Ha — everyone says my dad, and it's so annoying.

wrong.t: I am most similar to my father.
wrong.why: That's the answer, stated stiffly. The reaction is how you feel about it.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: We've got the same laugh, the same terrible jokes and the same obsession with Marítimo.
Mind you, if I'm honest, I'd rather be like him than anyone else.

wrong.t: Mind you, he also supports Marítimo.
wrong.why: That's another similarity. 'Mind you' should turn the answer.

wrong.t: On the other hand, my mother is also nice.
wrong.why: Changes the subject instead of turning the feeling.

alts.frame: Hmm, probably my ___, actually. She ___ when I was little, and she taught me ___ before I could even ___. We're both quite ___, but we ___.
alts.why: A hesitation, a surprising answer, a detail with a comparison in it. The reason is about character, not appearance.

segs.t: Hmm, probably my grandma, actually.

wrong.t: Definitely, one hundred per cent, my grandma!
wrong.why: Too certain for a surprising answer. 'Probably… actually' sounds like you're thinking.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: She moved in with us when I was little, and she taught me to cook before I could even ride a bike.
We're both quite quiet, but we notice everything. My family calls us 'the detectives'.

wrong.t: She taught me to cook when I was young.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Grandparents play an important role in Portuguese families.
wrong.why: A sociology point. Why are YOU like her?

cards.question: Do you go on holiday with your family?

alts.frame: Yes, but we usually stay on the island. Last summer we spent ___ in ___ and ___ every day. We don't go abroad very often, because ___.
alts.why: Answer, one real holiday, then the honest 'but'. That's the shape of your B2 column, without the stray 'here's.

segs.t: Yes, but we usually stay on the island.
Last summer we spent a week in Porto Moniz and swam in the natural pools every day.

wrong.t: For example, we go on holiday in Madeira.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Porto Moniz is in the north-west of the island.
wrong.why: Geography, not a memory.

segs.t: We don't go abroad very often, because flights from here are so expensive.

wrong.t: We also go to the beach a lot.
wrong.why: Adds, doesn't turn.

wrong.t: Nevertheless, domestic tourism has several advantages.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: Not as much as I'd like to! My parents both work in ___, so ___ is their busiest time. So we go away in ___ instead — which sounds weird, but at least ___.
alts.why: 'Not as much as I'd like' is a reaction and an answer in one. The 'weird, but' ending turns a complaint into something good.

segs.t: Not as much as I'd like to!

wrong.t: No.
wrong.why: A closed door. React with the feeling behind it.

wrong.t: Holidays are important for families.
wrong.why: A general statement, not a reaction.

segs.t: My parents both work in hotels, so summer is their busiest time.
So we go away in November instead — which sounds weird, but at least the beaches in Porto Santo are completely empty.

wrong.t: So we don't go on holiday in summer.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: However, the hotel industry is essential to Madeira's economy.
wrong.why: True, but now you're writing an essay about tourism.

alts.frame: Yeah, every ___ we fly to ___ to see ___. It's the only time the whole family is together, so it's ___ but ___. Last year ___, and ___!
alts.why: Reason plus a funny example. The example does the proving — you don't need to say 'it's chaotic', you show it.

segs.t: Yeah, every August we fly to Lisbon to see my cousins.
It's the only time the whole family is together, so it's chaotic but amazing.

wrong.t: We go to Lisbon because my cousins live in Lisbon.
wrong.why: Circular — it repeats the answer.

wrong.t: Lisbon is a beautiful and historic city.
wrong.why: About Lisbon, not about why the trip matters.

segs.t: Last year there were fourteen of us in one flat, and we had to take turns in the shower!

wrong.t: For example, we visit lots of places in Lisbon.
wrong.why: Vague. One moment you could film.

wrong.t: My cousins are the same age as me.
wrong.why: A fact, not a moment.

cards.question: Who do you spend time with at the weekend?

alts.frame: My ___, mostly — it's a very Madeiran thing! Every Sunday we have ___ at ___. It can get a bit ___, to be honest, but I'd really miss it if ___.
alts.why: A reaction with a smile, a fact, then a mixed feeling. 'I'd miss it if we stopped' is a second conditional doing emotional work.

segs.t: My family, mostly — it's a very Madeiran thing!

wrong.t: I spend time with my family here at weekends.
wrong.why: Your table's version — but the stray 'here' is a habit to avoid, and it's the answer, not a reaction.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: Every Sunday we have a massive lunch at my grandparents' house in Câmara de Lobos.
It can get a bit boring, to be honest, but I'd really miss it if we stopped.

wrong.t: It's also really delicious and fun.
wrong.why: No turn. Where's the other side?

wrong.t: However, some teenagers prefer to spend time with friends.
wrong.why: About 'some teenagers', not you.

alts.frame: My friends, definitely. On ___ we meet at ___ and just ___ for hours. It sounds pointless, but it's the only time we can ___. Last Saturday we ___ and bought absolutely nothing.
alts.why: 'It sounds pointless, but…' defends your answer before the examiner can judge it. The example is a punchline.

segs.t: My friends, definitely. On Saturdays we meet at Forum Madeira and just walk around for hours.
It sounds pointless, but it's the only time we can talk without our parents listening.

wrong.t: We go to Forum Madeira because it's a shopping centre.
wrong.why: Obvious. Why do you go?

wrong.t: Shopping centres are popular places for young people.
wrong.why: A general fact, not your reason.

segs.t: Last Saturday we spent three hours there and bought absolutely nothing.

wrong.t: For example, there are many shops there.
wrong.why: About the place, not about a Saturday.

wrong.t: We like shopping very much.
wrong.why: A feeling, not a moment.

alts.frame: It depends on the weekend. Every other Saturday I stay with my ___ in ___, because ___. It used to feel strange, but now I actually like ___!
alts.why: 'Used to… but now' tells a change in one breath. Serious content, light ending — that's complex without being heavy.

segs.t: It depends on the weekend.

wrong.t: I spend time with different people.
wrong.why: Vague, and it isn't a reaction. 'It depends' buys time naturally.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: Every other Saturday I stay with my dad in Machico, because my parents are separated.
It used to feel strange, but now I actually like having two homes — double the birthday presents!

wrong.t: It is strange to have two homes.
wrong.why: Stops at the hard part. The 'but now' is what shows how you feel today.

wrong.t: Divorce is increasingly common in modern society.
wrong.why: An essay sentence. Keep it about you.
